idea: Transition strategy advisory for industrial corporates
buyer: CFOs and strategy directors at mid-cap industrials
pain: They must show investors a credible transition plan and cannot build one
v1: A transition plan with investor-grade financials for one corporate
channel: Her investor network as referrers, corporates as buyers
verdict: Highest fees available and only four clients needed, but corporates are a cold, slow segment.

why.distribution: Corporates are not her network; she would rely on investor referrals into a cold segment.
why.demand: Corporates are spending on transition planning under investor and regulatory pressure.
why.fmf: Knowing exactly what investors want to see in a transition plan is a genuine and rare advantage.
why.revenue_structure: Large one-off engagements with possible annual refresh.
why.defensibility: Big consultancies dominate; her investor perspective is the differentiator.
why.tailwind: Transition disclosure requirements are tightening with real budget attached.
why.ceiling: £45k x 5 engagements = £225k, needing only five clients.

ceiling_arithmetic: £45k x 5 engagements = £225k gross, negligible direct cost. Only five clients needed, which is the appeal. But each is a 6-9 month corporate sale. Realistic year one: 1-2 = £45-90k.
carries: The highest fee per engagement in the set with only five clients needed, and a genuinely differentiated investor lens.
kills: Distribution. Corporates are cold, procurement is slow, and Big Four firms are already inside them.
test: Ask three investor contacts to name a portfolio company struggling with its transition plan, and request a referral.
test_pass: One referral converts to a scoping meeting.
